To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mechanical strength of the quartz-glass waveguides is determined primarily by the strength of the quartz glass, and the polymer cladding is a secondary factor.
the breaking strength of the waveguides investigated is determined by the mechanical strength of their quartz glass cores, which are of the same quality as the glass used to manufacture the fibers.

the strength of fiber-optics waveguides is comparable to that of quartz glass, and that the strength of waveguides with an optically reflecting polymer cladding can be increased by applying the cladding to the fiber during drawing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanical strength of waveguides, which is an extremely important factor for their application in optical communications systems.
the development of a method for increasing the strength of fiber-optical waveguides by means of a polymer coating.
the development of fiber-optic communication systems with high transmission capacity and high reliability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the breaking strength of quartz-glass fibers is higher than the breaking strength of polymer fibers, and the breaking strength of fibers having a polymer coating, deposited during the drawing process and having a thickness of 0.5 to 1 micron, is higher than the strength of fibers having an external coating of the same polymer.
the mechanical strength of quartz-glass waveguides with an optically reflecting polymer cladding is higher than that of the same fibers with an optically transparent polymer coating.
the strength of fiber-optics waveguides is determined by the strength of the quartz-glass core.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the breaking strength of the fiber-optic waveguide is not a critical parameter for the design of the optical communications system. the strength of fiber-optics waveguides can be improved by the application of a thin protective coating of a silicone polymer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high mechanical strength can be attained in fiber-optic waveguide materials by the method of deposition from the gased phase.
the breaking strength of waveguides can be increased to a level that is adequate for use in optical communication systems.
the strength of fiber-optical waveguides can be improved by increasing the drawing speed and decreasing the drawing temperature.
